[[File:Curtiss Murphy portrait.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Curtiss Murphy.]]
'''Curtiss Murphy''' is the namesake of [[Pucumir Thryss]], a [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] card whose name uses exactly the letters of his.<ref name="geo">[https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians] at oocities.org (GeoCities mirror). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008200413/https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> In 1998 he was a ranked Star Wars CCG tournament player in Virginia,<ref name="apptech">[http://www.app-tech.com/staff/cmurphy/ The Murphy Home Page], Appropriate Technologies, Inc. staff page (last revised 15 May 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000823153412/http://www.app-tech.com:80/staff/cmurphy/ Internet Archive]</ref> and he later said he had been a playtester for [[Decipher]].<ref name="gdz015">[https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/015-failure-taste-and-the-closet-star-wars-geek-the/id1028932466?i=1000358988905 015 : Failure, Taste, and the Closet Star Wars Geek – the Season 1 Finale], ''Game Design Zen'' podcast, Curtiss Murphy (15 December 2015), Zen Moment, 25:29–28:18 (show notes: "Star Wars – Pucumir Thryss – Anagram of me!"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027202348/https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/015-failure-taste-and-the-closet-star-wars-geek-the/id1028932466?i=1000358988905 Internet Archive]</ref>

== Star Wars CCG ==

In May 1998 his staff home page at Appropriate Technologies, Inc. in Chesapeake, Virginia, called him "a very competitive player of the Star Wars collectible card game" and said that "through well more than 100 sanctioned games I have gotten myself into the top 30 players in the world (currently there are over 20,350 ranked players)".<ref name="apptech" /> On 1 April 1998 he posted the deck [[Curtiss Murphy Ties in the Dark|Ties in the Dark]] to Decipher's [[Decipher swccg-discussion list archive|swccg-discussion]] list, writing that it had beaten SITDD "2 out of 3 times in sanctioned play".<ref name="list-36982">[http://groups.yahoo.com:80/group/swccg-discussion/message/36982 swccg-discussion message #36982], [[Curtiss Murphy]] (1 April 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010508200853/http://groups.yahoo.com:80/group/swccg-discussion/message/36982 Internet Archive]</ref>

In a December 2015 episode of his podcast ''Game Design Zen'', Murphy said that because Decipher was based in his home area on the east coast of Virginia, he got to know the company and became a playtester, helping "to improve the designs of their card game". He said that for an expansion with many characters who had no official names, Decipher "took some of the names of the senior play testers, made anagrams of them", and that Pucumir Thryss was his.<ref name="gdz015" /> No Decipher source records why the card carries his name, and the fan anagram list leaves his relation to Decipher as "????".<ref name="geo" />

== Career ==

Murphy studied at Virginia Tech.<ref name="li">[https://www.linkedin.com/in/curtissmurphy Curtiss Murphy], LinkedIn profile, read 27 October 2026 (public view: "MobilityWare"; Education: "Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University"; "Irvine, California, United States"; Publications: "Believable Dead Reckoning for Networked Games", Game Engine Gems 2, March 1, 2011, and "Designing and developing effective training games for the US Navy", M&S Journal, Apr 2012; Projects: "The Game Design Zen Podcast", Jul 2015). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027202123/https://swccg.com/snapshots/linkedin/curtissmurphy.html Internet Archive]</ref> In April 1998 he signed his posts as a senior software engineer at Appropriate Technologies, Inc.,<ref name="list-36982" /> and by May 1998 he was the company's Director of Product Development.<ref name="apptech" /> He later worked on training games and game technology, writing the chapter "Believable Dead Reckoning for Networked Games" in ''Game Engine Gems 2'' (2011), and in July 2015 he started the ''Game Design Zen'' podcast.<ref name="li" /> He became Vice President of Engineering at a major mobile game publisher,<ref name="scribe">[https://scribemedia.com/authors/curtiss-murphy Curtiss Murphy], Scribe Media author page (author of ''What Makes Great Managers Great''; "Vice President of Engineering", "Professor of Game Design at Laguna College of Art and Design"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027202320/https://scribemedia.com/authors/curtiss-murphy Internet Archive]</ref> MobilityWare in Irvine, California,<ref name="li" /> and taught game design at the Laguna College of Art and Design.<ref name="scribe" /><ref name="lcad">[https://www.lcad.edu/faculty/curtiss-murphy/ Curtiss Murphy], Laguna College of Art and Design faculty page ("Adjunct Faculty", Game Development Faculty). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260521070322/https://www.lcad.edu/faculty/curtiss-murphy/ Internet Archive]</ref> He is the author of the management book ''What Makes Great Managers Great''.<ref name="scribe" />
